Docs.summary: Marks an eligible native method to use the fastest available Java Native Interface (JNI) transitions.

remarks.para: A critical native method must be static, may have only primitive parameter types, and must return a primitive type or void. The annotation changes the JNI transition ABI, so the native implementation must omit the JNIEnv and jclass parameters.

While a critical native method executes, garbage collection cannot suspend its thread and may be blocked. Do not use this annotation on long-running methods or methods that perform significant I/O or acquire native locks that can be held for a long time. This annotation has no effect on non-native methods.

This optimization is a CTS-tested public API starting in Android 14. For maximum compatibility, avoid calling critical native methods on Android 13 and earlier. Dynamic JNI linking works only on Android 12 and later; methods used on Android 8 through Android 11 must be explicitly registered with JNI RegisterNatives. On Android 7 and earlier, the annotation is ignored, so the resulting ABI mismatch can cause incorrect argument marshalling and crashes.
